newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends nearly flat in frozen sentiment.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends nearly flat in frozen sentiment.

text.p: The won ended Friday's cautious trading nearly flat against the dollar on fears that the central Bank of Korea (BOK) would intervene to block any falls in the local currency, dealers said.
The won ended at 828.80 after opening at 829.00. It ranged from 828.20 and 829.20.
"The market is very quiet because no one wants to break the support line the BOK has set," said a local bank dealer.
Traders said the BOK intervened earlier this week when the won dropped below the 830 level. But the central bank has never acknowledged that it steps into the interbank market.
"But the dollar is still bullish because of fundamental factors like the trade deficit and the weak economy, so the market may test 830 again next week," said a First National Bank of Chicago dealer.
Import account settlements expected on Tuesday was also seen boosting the dollar, traders said.

The Chicago Bank dealer put next week's range between 825 and 830, while the local dealer said he saw it moving in a 828-830 range. "But if the market breaks the 830 level, it could rise as high as 835," he added.
